notes: ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός: the first article is emptied by the possessive on μου (rule 20) and the second is the unrepresented attributive article (rule 23) — two different reasons for the same status.
'While … yet speaking' splits ἔτι from λαλοῦντος, the genitive-absolute participle keeping the supplied subordinator and copula (rules 15, 86) while αὐτοῦ keeps 'he'.
εὐδόκησα heads on 'pleased', the lexical predicate, not on the subject or copula (rule 17).
